retroactive_finding_note: Running the current checker on this file reports `senior_review_missing` for B1 (`touches ci-gates; an independent reviewer with senior: true is required before merge`), so it prints TEAM_PLAN_FAIL. That finding is retroactive. The `ci-gates` risk family was widened on 2026-09-28 (commit 05b6cf8) to cover every file under `scripts/`; when this plan ran and shipped as PR #90 on 2026-09-25, `ci-gates` meant `.github/workflows/` only, so B1's grant of `scripts/render_brand_assets.cjs` and the browser-proof scripts `scripts/ux_polish_round2_browser_proof.cjs`, `scripts/r7r8_browser_proof.cjs` and `scripts/p0_browser_proof.cjs` was standard-risk work, no senior reviewer was required, and none was appointed: R1 was an ordinary independent read-only review. This record is deliberately NOT edited to make the checker pass. Setting `senior: true` on R1, or adding a reviewer row, would assert that a senior review happened when it did not; a fabricated reviewer inside a historic record is a worse outcome than a known failing check, and the next agent to read this file should leave the failure standing. The same run also reports six `open_work_overlap` findings for B1 and B2 against `origin/codex/senior-engineering-review-20260921` and `origin/chatgpt/phone-team-gpt6-openai-only-20260923`: those are recomputed from live git state on every run, so they describe today's branches rather than the state at dispatch, they were already accepted and recorded in PROJECT_STATUS.md when this plan ran (`TEAM_PLAN_FAIL accepted and recorded: only the stale PR #71 and two status-only branches overlap, none on shared lines`), and the `plan.accepted_overlaps` field that would record them inside the plan did not exist on 2026-09-25. The decision to pay the `ci-gates` cost rather than hide it is recorded in the `claude` slot of PROJECT_STATUS.md, in the 2026-09-28 orchestration-enforcement round-two entry that names this file and docs/team-plans/2026-09-24-daylight-visual-refresh.json as the deliberate over-inclusion and explains why a name-keyword allowlist was rejected. Nothing in CI is red because of this: no CI step runs the checker over committed plans.
